lesson.subject: anatomy
lesson.title: Abdominal lymphatics and autonomic pathways
lesson.summary: A plexus mixes fibers with different directions and functions.
lesson.section: 32. Abdominal Lymphatics; 33. Autonomic Innervation of Abdominal Viscera

steps.title: Abdominal Lymphatics
steps.body:
Abdominal lymph drainage follows arteries toward pre-aortic nodes for gut organs and para-aortic nodes for posterior abdominal wall and paired retroperitoneal organs. Lymph eventually reaches intestinal and lumbar trunks and cisterna chyli.

Foregut lymph drains toward celiac nodes. Midgut lymph drains toward superior mesenteric nodes. Hindgut lymph drains toward inferior mesenteric nodes. Kidneys, gonads, suprarenal glands, and posterior abdominal wall drain toward lumbar/para-aortic nodes. Cisterna chyli receives intestinal and lumbar trunks and continues as thoracic duct.

steps.title: Autonomic Innervation of Abdominal Viscera
steps.body:
Abdominal viscera receive sympathetic and parasympathetic fibers through prevertebral plexuses. Sympathetic fibers travel mainly through thoracic and lumbar splanchnic nerves; parasympathetic fibers come from vagus nerve and pelvic splanchnic nerves.

Vagus supplies parasympathetic innervation to foregut and midgut derivatives up to proximal transverse colon. Pelvic splanchnic nerves S2-S4 supply parasympathetic innervation to hindgut derivatives from distal transverse colon onward. Sympathetic efferents generally reduce gut motility and constrict vessels. Visceral pain afferents often accompany sympathetic routes but are distinct sensory fibers. Visceral afferent pain localization follows embryologic origin: foregut epigastric, midgut periumbilical, hindgut hypogastric.

steps.title: Where do autonomic fibers synapse, and why is the distinction useful?
steps.body: Many sympathetic preganglionic fibers reach prevertebral ganglia, after which postganglionic fibers follow arterial routes to viscera. Parasympathetic fibers generally synapse near or within the organ in enteric or terminal ganglia. Enteric circuits coordinate local motility and secretion while receiving autonomic modulation. Thus a plexus near an artery contains a mixture of passing fibers and ganglionic structures rather than one uniform neuron type. Sensory afferents returning from viscera must be kept distinct from either autonomic motor pathway.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: A plexus mixes fibers with different directions and functions. Sympathetic efferents reach prevertebral ganglia through splanchnic routes, while visceral afferents often travel alongside them in the opposite direction. Vagal parasympathetic supply extends through the midgut; pelvic splanchnics serve the hindgut. Lymphatic vessels are a separate transport system, often following arterial routes toward regional nodes. Sharing an anatomical corridor does not make nerve, blood and lymph pathways interchangeable.
